decisions.title: Use Prisma SQLite for Local and Prisma Neon PostgreSQL for Staging/Production
decisions.context: Local development was previously planned around a dedicated Neon PostgreSQL project, which introduced NEON_API_KEY/project-provisioning requirements before the Shopify Dev app could run. The project owner has chosen a Shopify-default-style Local workflow: Prisma with a local SQLite database, while Staging and Production continue using isolated Neon PostgreSQL through the cloud Prisma schema.
alternatives: Keep dedicated Neon PostgreSQL for Local, Staging and Production.
Use a locally installed PostgreSQL server for Local and Neon PostgreSQL for hosted environments.
Use Prisma SQLite for Local and Prisma Neon PostgreSQL for Staging/Production.
evidence_refs: Current Local Neon preparation blocker requiring NEON_API_KEY
decisions.decision: Local/Dev will use Prisma with a gitignored SQLite database and the dedicated VSN | Stock Down Sort Dev Shopify app. Staging and Production will continue using Prisma with isolated Neon PostgreSQL databases and the cloud schema. Local acceptance proves application/session/data-flow behavior on SQLite; it does not count as PostgreSQL acceptance. Staging remains the mandatory first real PostgreSQL/Neon acceptance gate before any Production preparation.
consequences: Local development no longer requires NEON_API_KEY, NEON_PROJECT_ID, Neon project provisioning, or cloud database credentials.
The repository must maintain a Local SQLite Prisma schema/migration path and a hosted PostgreSQL Prisma schema/migration path.
Shared data models must be covered by a schema-parity contract so Local and cloud schemas do not silently drift.
Provider-specific PostgreSQL behavior must be verified in Staging before Production.
The existing Local Neon scripts/guards must be removed or retired only after the SQLite conversion is implemented and CI-validated.
Staging and Production Neon architecture, manual promotion gates, and billing isolation remain unchanged.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: Reduces Local secret exposure by removing Neon account/project credentials from the developer workstation workflow.
Keeps Staging and Production database credentials isolated in their existing environment scopes.
Local SQLite files must remain gitignored and must never be committed.
Reduces cloud dependency and cost/availability coupling for normal Local development.
decisions.reversibility: reversible through a later accepted ADR and migration work unit

rules: Accepted material decisions must not be silently reversed.
A replacement decision must preserve supersession traceability.
Decision evidence must distinguish verified facts from inference.
